original_value: Image classification is a fundamental task in remote sensing image processing. In recent years, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have experienced significant breakthroughs in natural image recognition. The remote sensing field, is still lacking a large-scale benchmark similar to ImageNet. In this paper, we propose a remote sensing image classification benchmark (RSI-CB) based on massive, scalable, and diverse crowdsourced data. Using crowdsourced data, such as Open Street Map (OSM) data, ground objects in remote sensing images can be annotated effectively using points of interest, vector data from OSM, or other crowdsourced data. These annotated images can, then, be used in remote sensing image classification tasks. Based on this method, we construct a worldwide large-scale benchmark for remote sensing image classification. This benchmark has large-scale geographical distribution and large total image number. It contains six categories with 35 sub-classes of more than 24,000 images of size 256 × 256 pixels. This classification system of ground objects is defined according to the national standard of land-use classification in China and is inspired by the hierarchy mechanism of ImageNet. Finally, we conduct numerous experiments to compare RSI-CB with the SAT-4, SAT-6, and UC-Merced data sets. The experiments show that RSI-CB is more suitable as a benchmark for remote sensing image classification tasks than other benchmarks in the big data era and has many potential applications.

result.paraphrase: Image classification is a core task in remote sensing image processing. In recent years, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have made major advances in natural image recognition. However, the remote sensing field still lacks a large-scale benchmark comparable to ImageNet. In this paper, we introduce a remote sensing image classification benchmark (RSI-CB) built from massive, scalable, and diverse crowdsourced data. With crowdsourced sources such as Open Street Map (OSM) data, ground objects in remote sensing images can be effectively annotated using points of interest, OSM vector data, or other crowdsourced information. These labeled images can then be used for remote sensing image classification tasks. Using this approach, we create a worldwide large-scale benchmark for remote sensing image classification. It features broad geographic coverage and a large total number of images. The benchmark includes six categories and 35 sub-classes, with more than 24,000 images sized 256 × 256 pixels. Its ground-object classification system follows the national standard for land-use classification in China and draws on the hierarchical structure of ImageNet. Finally, we perform extensive experiments comparing RSI-CB with the SAT-4, SAT-6, and UC-Merced data sets. The results indicate that RSI-CB is better suited than the other benchmarks for remote sensing image classification in the big data era and offers many potential applications.
